question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt this hybrid legacy-root plus named-account configuration, including inherited shared settings and per-account identity, webhook, credential, and state rules, as its permanent public contract?
rationale: The implementation is technically strong, but these inheritance and upgrade semantics become a durable configuration and operational contract that automation cannot approve safely.

options.title: Approve Hybrid Contract
options.body: Retain the legacy root shape as the default account, add named accounts using generic bindings, and land after owner review and green exact-head validation.

options.title: Require Explicit Accounts
options.body: Move all Teams identities under `accounts` and provide a doctor migration, accepting a larger compatibility and documentation burden.

options.title: Defer Multi-Account Teams
options.body: Pause or close the contribution until maintainers select a different permanent account model.

recommendation.title: Approve Hybrid Contract
recommendation.body: Retain the legacy root shape as the default account, add named accounts using generic bindings, and land after owner review and green exact-head validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal spans the Teams plugin and the shared channel contracts this decision affects.
